findings.title: Could not establish a TLS connection on port 443
findings.description: No TLS handshake could be completed with the server on port 443. Either the site is HTTP-only, or the TLS stack is misconfigured.
findings.impact: All traffic - including logins and payment data - travels unencrypted.
findings.remediation: Install a valid certificate (Let's Encrypt is free) and serve the site exclusively over HTTPS.
evidence: Error: [WinError 10061] No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it

findings.title: Missing Anti-CSRF Protection on State-Changing Form
findings.description: A sensitive POST form at action 'http://127.0.0.1:8099/login' on page http://127.0.0.1:8099/ does not contain an anti-Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) token.
findings.description_bn: http://127.0.0.1:8099/ পেজের ফর্মে কোনো CSRF প্রটেকশন টোকেন নেই।
findings.impact: An attacker can host a malicious webpage that silently submits requests on behalf of authenticated users without their consent, potentially altering account details, emails, or settings.
findings.impact_bn: অন্য কোনো ক্ষতিকর ওয়েবসাইট থেকে ব্যবহারকারীর অজান্তেই প্রোফাইল আপডেট বা পাসওয়ার্ড পরিবর্তন করে ফেলা সম্ভব।
findings.remediation: Implement unpredictable, cryptographically strong anti-CSRF synchronizer tokens for all state-changing POST/PUT/DELETE requests. Additionally, configure session cookies with `SameSite=Lax` or `SameSite=Strict`.

fix_patches.code:
<!-- Include CSRF Token in Form -->
<form method="POST" action="/account/update">
  <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token }}">
  <!-- inputs -->
</form>

findings.title: Directory listing is enabled
findings.description: The web server returns an auto-generated file index for http://127.0.0.1:8099/uploads/. Visitors can browse the contents of these folders directly, including files that were never meant to be linked.
findings.impact: Disclosure of uploaded documents, backups, temporary files and sometimes personal data belonging to other users.
findings.remediation:
Disable autoindex:
nginx: autoindex off;
Apache: Options -Indexes
and move non-public files outside the web root.

findings.title: Open redirect via parameter 'url'
findings.description: The 'url' parameter controls where the user is sent, and it accepts any external host. The application will happily redirect visitors to an attacker-controlled site while the link still starts with your domain.
findings.impact: Highly effective phishing: 'https://yourdomain/login?next=evil.com' looks trustworthy, and is also used to steal OAuth tokens and bypass allow-lists.
findings.remediation: Accept only relative paths, or validate against an allow-list of permitted hosts before redirecting. Reject values containing '://' and '//'.

findings.title: Outdated jQuery 1.12.4 (known XSS issues)
findings.description: jQuery 1.12.4 predates fixes for CVE-2020-11022 / CVE-2020-11023 (XSS via htmlPrefilter) and, below 3.4.0, CVE-2019-11358 (prototype pollution in jQuery.extend).
findings.impact: Untrusted HTML passed to .html()/.append() can execute script, re-enabling XSS even where the application escapes correctly.
findings.remediation: Upgrade to jQuery 3.7.x and audit any .html() call that receives user data.

findings.title: Absence of Rate Limiting on Authentication Endpoint
findings.title_bn: অথেনটিকেশন এন্ডপয়েন্টে রেট লিমিটিং (Rate Limiting) এর অভাব
findings.description: The authentication endpoint at http://127.0.0.1:8099/login showed no evidence of rate limiting or brute-force throttling after rapid successive queries (no 429 status code or standard RateLimit-* headers detected).
findings.description_bn: http://127.0.0.1:8099/login এ কোনো রেট লিমিটিং নেই, ফলে হ্যাকাররা স্বয়ংক্রিয়ভাবে হাজার হাজার পাসওয়ার্ড ট্রাই করতে পারবে।
findings.impact: Allows malicious actors to perform automated credential stuffing, dictionary password attacks, or distributed brute-force attacks against user accounts without triggering throttling.
findings.impact_bn: সহজেই ব্রুট-ফোর্স (Brute-Force) বা ক্রেডেনশিয়াল স্টাফিং অ্যাটাক চালিয়ে ইউজারের অ্যাকাউন্ট হ্যাক করা সম্ভব।
findings.remediation: Enforce strict IP and account-based rate limiting on all login, registration, and password recovery endpoints. Return HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) with a `Retry-After` header when thresholds are exceeded. Implement account lockouts or progressive CAPTCHA challenges after consecutive failed attempts.
evidence: Tested 6 rapid requests; all returned status 404
findings.poc_curl: for i in {1..10}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' 'http://127.0.0.1:8099/login'; done

findings.title: CSP has no frame-ancestors directive
findings.description: frame-ancestors is the modern replacement for X-Frame-Options. Its absence means clickjacking protection depends on a legacy header alone.
findings.remediation: Add frame-ancestors 'self' (or 'none' where framing is not needed).

findings.title: External links open with target=_blank but no rel=noopener
findings.description: A link opened in a new tab keeps a reference to your page through window.opener. The destination site can use it to redirect the original tab to a phishing page.
findings.impact: Users who return to the original tab land on an attacker-controlled clone.
findings.remediation: Add rel="noopener noreferrer" to every target="_blank" link, or set it globally in the framework.

findings.title: HTML comments reveal internal information
findings.description: Developer comments are shipped to production. They often contain credentials, internal hostnames, TODO notes about unpatched areas, or hints about hidden admin paths.
findings.impact: Free reconnaissance for an attacker, sometimes including direct credentials.
findings.remediation: Strip comments in the build step (HTML minification does this automatically) and review what is deployed.
evidence: <!-- TODO: remove test admin:admin before launch -->

findings.title: Technology versions disclosed in response headers
findings.description: Response headers advertise the exact server and framework versions. An attacker can match these against public CVE databases and pick exploits that are known to work, skipping the reconnaissance phase entirely.
findings.impact: Faster, more reliable targeting of version-specific vulnerabilities.
findings.remediation: Suppress or genericise version strings: nginx `server_tokens off;`, Apache `ServerTokens Prod` / `ServerSignature Off`, PHP `expose_php = Off`, and remove X-Powered-By at the reverse proxy.

findings.title: Third-party scripts loaded without Subresource Integrity
findings.description: 1 script tag(s) load code from an external host without an integrity hash. If that CDN or vendor is compromised, the modified script runs with full access to your users' sessions.
findings.impact: One compromised third-party host becomes a compromise of your site.
findings.remediation:
Add integrity and crossorigin attributes:
<script src="https://cdn.example/lib.js" integrity="sha384-..." crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
findings.owasp: A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures

findings.title: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy (COOP) header is missing
findings.description: COOP isolates your browsing context from cross-origin windows, closing cross-window attacks such as Spectre-style leaks and tabnabbing chains.
findings.impact: Raises the likelihood and blast radius of any injection flaw on the site; an attacker who lands one script gets a durable foothold in users' browsers.
evidence: Response headers did not include: cross-origin-opener-policy

findings.title: No web application firewall detected
findings.description: No WAF or CDN filtering layer was identified in front of the application. Nothing sits between the internet and the code to block obvious attack patterns.
findings.impact: Every malicious request reaches the application directly; there is no virtual patching option when a CVE drops.
findings.remediation: Consider a WAF/CDN (Cloudflare, AWS WAF, or a managed service). Treat it as defence in depth only - it never replaces fixing the underlying code.

findings.title: Password field allows browser autocomplete
findings.description: The login form does not set autocomplete="off" or a credential-manager hint. On shared devices this can leave credentials stored in the browser.
findings.impact: Minor credential exposure on shared computers.
findings.remediation: Use autocomplete="current-password" on login and "new-password" on registration so password managers behave correctly, and avoid autocomplete="off" on login (it breaks managers).

findings.title: robots.txt points at sensitive paths
findings.description: robots.txt lists directories that look sensitive. Bots ignore this file, and it is often the first thing an attacker reads - it works as a signpost rather than a control.
findings.impact: Guides attackers to admin, backup or internal paths.
findings.remediation: Do not rely on robots.txt for access control. Protect these paths with real authentication and remove the hints.
